deep.reconstruction:
There are no derivations on this page. It is a dated reading list headed 'Gelesene Bücher' (books read), covering October 1855 to January 1856. An earlier heading ('Gelesene Bücher / 1855. Weimar') is crossed out at the top. Entries in order:

(1) 1855 October. 'Weimar' (underlined): 'Anweisungen für Jünglinge zum eigenen Arbeiten, besonders zum Lesen, Excerpiren, und Schreiben'. This is a study-skills manual for young men on reading, excerpting and writing. 'Weimar' is probably the place of publication. I could not identify the author.

(2) Lamé, 'Théorie mathématique de l'élasticité des corps solides'. This is Lamé's 'Leçons sur la théorie mathématique de l'élasticité des corps solides' (1852). Note: begun Easter 1855.

(3) Kummer, the first three memoirs on ideal complex numbers ('idealen complexen Primzahlen'). The references are given to Crelle's Journal vol. 30 and vol. 35 with further numbers ('7', '15', '16') and '§ 1-7'. These are Kummer's 1846-47 cyclotomic ideal-number papers, chiefly the Crelle 35 memoirs 'Zur Theorie der complexen Zahlen' and 'Über die Zerlegung der aus Wurzeln der Einheit gebildeten complexen Zahlen in ihre Primfactoren'. The exact citation numbers are hard to read.

(4) Brewster, 'Newton's Life', either Life of Newton (1831) or Memoirs of Newton (1855).

(5) Albrecht von Haller, 'Gedichte'.

(6) Arago, 'Oeuvres complètes', vols. 1-3. These are the 'Notices biographiques' volumes, 1854-55.

(7) 'Herbart' (underlined). Probably Herbart's works, which fits the Herbart excerpts on the previous page.

(8) Leibniz, 'Opera omnia', ed. Dutens (1768), tomes I and II. Under it is Leibniz's 'Theoria motus abstracti' (1671).

(9) Added in the right margin: 'Nov.-December. Montucla, Histoire des mathématiques.' Below it: '[Leo?] (über Landen etc.)', a reading on John Landen, probably in connection with Landen's transformation of elliptic integrals.

(10) Abel, 'Oeuvres complètes', vols. 1 and 2 (Holmboe edition, 1839).

(11) 1856 January. Guhrauer, 'Leben Leibnitz's', i.e. G. E. Guhrauer's Leibniz biography (1842). The parenthesis reads '(Ms. v. Leibnitz)', possibly 'manuscripts of Leibniz'.

(12) Guhrauer, Habilitationsschrift on Leibniz, with the parenthesis '(Verh. zu Spinoza)', i.e. Leibniz's relation to Spinoza.

(13) 'Mémoires de l'ac. T. 11' with '(Preisschr. v. Rosenhain)'. This is Rosenhain's prize memoir on functions of two variables with four periods (genus-2 hyperelliptic theta functions). It was published in Mémoires présentés par divers savants à l'Académie des Sciences, t. 11 (1851).

Page number 175 is stamped at right.

Context: the list ties in with Riemann's Herbart and Leibniz studies (Naturphilosophie, previous page). It also ties in with his preparation of the 1857 'Theorie der Abel'schen Functionen' (Abel, Rosenhain, Landen/elliptic functions) and with his elasticity and physics interests (Lamé).

results.what: Record of Riemann's reading, Oct 1855 to Jan 1856. It shows study of Abel's Oeuvres and Rosenhain's genus-2 theta prize memoir shortly before his 1857 Abelian functions paper, alongside Kummer's ideal numbers, Lamé's elasticity, and Herbart/Leibniz philosophy.
results.modern_name: Biographical/bibliographical evidence (reading list); no mathematical result

deep.surprise_reason: This is a reading list with no mathematics. It is mildly interesting as a dating aid: it shows Abel and Rosenhain read just before 'Theorie der Abel'schen Functionen' (1857), plus Kummer and the Herbart/Leibniz influence. Riemann's engagement with Herbart, Abel and Rosenhain is already well documented, and lists of this kind are known to Riemann scholars.
transcription_corrections: 'Herbart.' (underlined) and 'Leibnitzii op. ed. Dutens. T I. II.' (separately underlined) look like two separate entries, Herbart and Leibniz. 'Theoria motus abstracti' belongs under the Leibniz entry.
'Abel. Oeuvres complètes. 1, 2.' matches the two-volume 1839 Holmboe edition; the image could be misread as '1,12'.

The margin entry reads 'Nov.-December. Montucla, Histoire des mathématiques.' followed on the next line by a short word (transcribed 'Leo', uncertain) and '(über Landen etc.)'. The word 'Leo' is doubtful.
The Kummer reference is approximately 'Crelle 30, [struck] 7. 35 15. 16; § 1-7'. The numbers are uncertain beyond the volume numbers 30 and 35.
'(Preisschr. v. Rosenhain)' is the prize memoir of J. G. Rosenhain in Mém. prés. div. sav. t. 11; the reading 'Preisschr.' is consistent with this.
The crossed-out header at the top reads '[-Gelesene Bücher-] [-1855. Weimar-]', with a correction above '1855'.
